text:
incident-bot: Paging: #incidents HelixBank private VPC — customer-reported inference endpoints returning 502/connection timeouts (impact: HelixBank prod, dedicated private pool). Paging oncall: @sanjay (severity: high)

sanjay (oncall): I'm on it. hitting HelixBank support channel to confirm impact. any alerts in console?

ops-bot: Alert: 3 hosts unhealthy in target group tg-helixbank-inference (NLB) in us-east-1. Error: TLS handshake failures and connection resets.

marta (sre): seeing elevated 502s in our metrics for HelixBank model route (route: /v1/helixbank/generate). Latency spikes then drops to 504/timeouts. Rolling windows show egress errors to customer internal endpoint.

dax (neteng): early hypothesis: health checks failing at NLB -> targets marked unhealthy -> requests blackholed. Could be SG or backend OS-level socket exhaustion. I can pull target health.

leo (platform): I can run `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg-helixbank-inference` and paste output.

leo (platform): ```json
{
  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [
    {"Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.5"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy","Reason": "TLS error"}},
    {"Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.6"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy","Reason": "Timeout"}},
    {"Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.7"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "healthy","Reason": "Ok"}}
  ]
}```

marta (sre): interesting — one healthy, others unhealthy. Any recent security group changes on the HelixBank VPC? 

emily (AM): HelixBank reported they pushed an ingress policy change to restrict pod egress to external vendor IPs about 30m ago. They said it was limited to app-tier but maybe affected inference. 

dax (neteng): if customer tightened security groups or NACLs and preserved client source IP, NLB target health checks from the LB subnet might be blocked. Need to verify SG rules on instances 10.0.12.5/6.

leo (platform): I can run a quick `ssh` into the node and `tcpdump` to see incoming health checks and TLS handshakes. On it.

leo (platform): `sudo tcpdump -n host 10.0.0.14 and port 443` shows SYN from NLB subnets but RST replies from instance on 10.0.12.6. Also kernel log shows `conntrack: expect NAT helper` errors.

marta (sre): conntrack errors could indicate ephemeral port exhaustion or misconfigured NAT rules—client-preserved source IPs mean conntrack shouldn't be needed unless proxying. What do service logs show?

leo (platform): Service logs: repeated `tls: handshake error from 10.0.1.45: remote error: tls: bad certificate` for target 10.0.12.5. For 10.0.12.6 I see `accept tcp 0.0.0.0:443: accept4: too many open files` sporadically.

sanjay (oncall): So two separate failures: TLS cert mismatch on one node and FD exhaustion on another. Could be config drift after deploy. Any recent deploys to HelixBank dedicated pool?

emily (AM): HelixBank confirmed they rotated internal certs and rolled a config change ~40m ago across their control plane. They said they excluded inference nodes but might have a partial rollout.

dax (neteng): Action plan: 1) Failover traffic away from unhealthy targets by registering a warm standby target or shifting NLB target group to healthy instance; 2) Ask HelixBank to relax SG for LB subnets to allow health checks temporarily; 3) If TLS certs are mismatch, fallback to plain TCP passthrough if possible.

marta (sre): I'll coordinate steps with HelixBank. @emily can you ask them to: a) confirm SG allows inbound from NLB subnets; b) confirm cert rotation state for service on inference nodes; c) allow short TTL DNS change if we need to swap to hosted endpoint?

emily (AM): pinged HelixBank support — they reply: "We accidentally applied a strict egress/ingress rule to inference nodes; will revert for LB subnets only for 15 mins." They also said cert rotation is halfway through; instances behind 10.0.12.5 still using old cert.

leo (platform): Ok, HelixBank reverted the SG rule for LB subnets. I see incoming health checks succeed for 10.0.12.5 now but still TLS mismatch until their certs finish rotating.

ops-bot: Audit: SG change detected on sg-helix-inference at 2026-09-18T15:12:09Z by user helix-admin: Removed restrictive rule allowing 10.0.0.0/16 from ALB/NLB subnets.

marta (sre): Good. Next, mitigate FD exhaustion on 10.0.12.6: I'd prefer rolling restart of inference process on that host and increase ulimit for open files. Leo, can you do a quick restart? If not possible, we'll drain and remove target then re-register.

leo (platform): Restarting inference service on 10.0.12.6 now: `sudo systemctl restart redwood-inference`

leo (platform): Service restarted, logs show `started` and FD usage dropped. Target health moved to healthy in ~12s.

dax (neteng): NLB target group now shows 3 healthy targets. I recommend keeping SG revert for 20m and then coordinate with HelixBank to re-run cert rotation but in a controlled canary.

emily (AM): HelixBank accepts: they'll re-run cert rotation on a single node and validate then proceed. They also asked for us to keep a fallback route to Redwood hosted API for critical traffic; we offered to failover to hosted for 15m while they finish rotation.

sanjay (oncall): Decide: 1) Keep current mitigations (SG revert + restart) and monitor for 15m. 2) Plan short DNS cutover to hosted route if we see repeat failures. I'll set an SLO and rollback window.

marta (sre): Monitoring: added short-lived alert to watch `helixbank-inference.502_rate` and `target_unhealthy_count`. If 502_rate > 5% sustained for 2m -> initiate DNS cutover.

incident-bot: Handoff scheduled: oncall rotation change in 25 minutes -> @dax will take lead for monitoring.

dax (neteng): I'm taking lead. I'll monitor NLB target health and TCP metrics. Also will coordinate with HelixBank network lead.

emily (AM): Customer update posted: "We've identified an ingress SG rule causing health checks to fail; we've temporarily reverted the rule and restarted service on affected nodes. HelixBank will re-run cert rotation in canary mode. Redwood is standing by to failover to hosted endpoints if necessary."

marta (sre): Post-incident actions noted: 1) run a playbook for cert rotations with HelixBank to avoid partial rollouts breaking TLS; 2) add SG preflight test to validate LB health check reachability before applying org-wide SG changes; 3) increase default ulimit on inference images.

sanjay (oncall): Closing loop: impact window ~15m, customer-facing errors reduced to <1% after mitigations. No data exfiltration. Will file postmortem and tag HelixBank account. Passing to @dax for next 2h watch.

dax (neteng): Acknowledged. I have the runbook open and will escalate to network infra if anything resurfaces.

incident-bot: Thread status: monitoring. Please update with any regressions. :white_check_mark:
